title: Founding of Baghdad
summary: Al-Mansur founds Baghdad as the Abbasid capital, soon a world city of learning and trade.
body: The round city sat on Tigris commerce. Translation movements and later libraries made it a symbol of the Islamic golden age—again a later phrase, but the concentration of scholarship was real. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.

sources.name: Kennedy, When Baghdad Ruled the Muslim World
